clinician.final_diagnosis: Compressive optic neuropathy (CON) secondary to thyroid eye disease with superior rectus and levator muscle inflammation and hypertrophy
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 66-year-old woman with 23-year history of hyperthyroidism treated with methimazole and potassium iodide presented with right upper eyelid retraction (MRD-1 3.2 mm). Initial examination showed normal exophthalmometry (13.5 mm right, 12.5 mm left) and no reported visual dysfunction. Thyroid labs demonstrated active hyperthyroidism (FT4 1.27 ng/dl, FT3 6.37 pg/ml, TSAb 1557%, TSH 0.008 μU/L). At 3 months, thyroid control worsened significantly (FT4 3.88 ng/dl, FT3 24.90 pg/ml, TSAb 3185%) with progression of eyelid retraction to MRD-1 7.3 mm. At 6 months, further progression occurred with MRD-1 7.7 mm, development of exotropia (12 PD) and hypertropia (20 PD). CT and MRI imaging revealed high degree of inflammation and hypertrophy of the superior rectus and upper levator muscles. Compressive optic neuropathy developed in the right eye with visual acuity declining to 20/200 and critical flicker fusion frequency of 16 Hz. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy (500 mg every 3 days for 2 weeks) and radiation therapy (20 Gy/10 fractions). Post-treatment imaging showed resolution of inflammation and visual acuity recovered to 20/20, though eyelid retraction (MRD-1 5.9 mm) and hypertropia (25 PD) persisted.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with right upper eyelid retraction
Active hyperthyroidism at initial presentation with elevated thyroid hormones and TSAb
Progressive worsening of thyroid control and eyelid retraction at 3 months
Further progression at 6 months with development of strabismus (exotropia and hypertropia)
CT and MRI imaging showing high degree of inflammation and hypertrophy of superior rectus and upper levator muscles
Development of compressive optic neuropathy with visual acuity decline to 20/200 and critical flicker fusion frequency 16 Hz
Treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy and radiation therapy resulting in resolution of inflammation and visual acuity recovery to 20/20
Persistent eyelid retraction and hypertropia after treatment despite visual acuity recovery

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Simple eyelid retraction without optic nerve involvement
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Progressive muscle inflammation on imaging and development of CON with visual acuity decline to 20/200 and abnormal critical flicker fusion frequency confirm optic nerve compression
Exophthalmometry remained normal (13.5 mm right, 12.5 mm left) throughout presentation, ruling out significant proptosis as the primary pathology
Imaging showed inflammation and hypertrophy of both superior rectus and levator muscles, and development of hypertropia and exotropia indicates extraocular muscle involvement beyond levator alone

remaining_uncertainties: Baseline visual acuity at initial presentation was not explicitly documented; only absence of reported visual dysfunction was noted
Specific optic disc findings (edema, pallor, or other signs) that confirmed CON diagnosis were not detailed in available records
Detailed extraocular motility examination findings at time of CON diagnosis were not provided
Specific timing of when visual acuity declined from baseline to 20/200 between 3-month and 6-month visits is not precisely documented
Whether any additional thyroid management changes were made during the treatment period beyond the documented steroid and radiation therapy

evaluation.known_final_diagnosis: As a result, CON developed in her right eye, and the corrected visual acuity in that eye was significantly reduced to 20/200 and the central critical flicker fusion frequency was 16 Hz. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans showed a high degree of inflammation and hypertrophy only in the superior rectus and upper levator muscles (Fig. 3).
